_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-06 01:22:37Z)**_

Here's what the issue would touch. Which files you need depends on one design decision.

**The decision:** every element already has a `link` field ([types.ts:79](packages/element/src/types.ts#L79)), and the existing link popup and click-through use it. So there are two ways to build this:

- **Option A, whole text box is the link.** When pasted text is a URL, set the new text element's `link` to it. The existing link UI then handles clicking through. This is small, but only fits text that is just a URL.
- **Option B, links inside the text.** Find URLs within a text element's content, draw them as links, and make only those characters clickable. This matches "medium" scope better and is more work.

### Files for both options

- [packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx): the paste handler (`pasteFromClipboard`, ~L4023). A URL your app accepts as embeddable currently becomes an embed instead of text (~L3983 and ~L12797), so you'll need to decide how those interact. Click handling also lives here.
- [packages/common/src/url.ts](packages/common/src/url.ts): checks and cleans up URLs (`toValidURL`, `normalizeLink`).
- [packages/excalidraw/wysiwyg/textWysiwyg.tsx](packages/excalidraw/wysiwyg/textWysiwyg.tsx): pasting a URL while editing a text box.
- [packages/element/src/newElement.ts](packages/element/src/newElement.ts): creating the text element with its link.
- [packages/excalidraw/components/hyperlink/Hyperlink.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/hyperlink/Hyperlink.tsx) and [helpers.ts](packages/excalidraw/components/hyperlink/helpers.ts): the existing link popup, link-icon hover and click-through.

### Extra files for Option B

- [packages/element/src/renderElement.ts](packages/element/src/renderElement.ts): drawing link text differently (color, underline).
- [packages/element/src/textMeasurements.ts](packages/element/src/textMeasurements.ts) and [textWrapping.ts](packages/element/src/textWrapping.ts): working out where a URL's characters land after line wrapping, so clicks can be matched to them.
- [packages/element/src/textElement.ts](packages/element/src/textElement.ts): a helper to find URLs in the text.
- [packages/element/src/collision.ts](packages/element/src/collision.ts): checking whether a click hit a URL's area.
- [packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticSvgScene.ts](packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticSvgScene.ts): keeping links clickable in SVG export.
- [packages/element/src/types.ts](packages/element/src/types.ts): only if you store link positions on the element rather than finding them each time.
- [packages/excalidraw/data/restore.ts](packages/excalidraw/data/restore.ts): only if you add a new field.

### Tests

- [packages/excalidraw/wysiwyg/textWysiwyg.test.tsx](packages/excalidraw/wysiwyg/textWysiwyg.test.tsx)
- [packages/common/tests/url.test.tsx](packages/common/tests/url.test.tsx)
- [packages/excalidraw/tests/clipboard.test.tsx](packages/excalidraw/tests/clipboard.test.tsx), if it exists; I haven't checked.

I found these by searching for names and haven't traced every call path, so expect one or two more files once you start building.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-06 01:32:22Z)**_

**What a field is:** a named property on an object. Every drawing element in Excalidraw is a plain object, and its type definition lists the fields it has. For example, [types.ts:79](packages/element/src/types.ts#L79) has `link: string | null`, so every element has a `link` field that holds one URL or nothing. Adding a field means adding a new line to that type, such as `textLinks`.

**Will the core link logic stay untouched?** Mostly, but your design runs into it in two places:

1. **Ctrl+K is already taken.** It opens the existing link editor for the whole element ([actionLink.tsx:40](packages/excalidraw/actions/actionLink.tsx#L40); it's also checked in [Hyperlink.tsx:272](packages/excalidraw/components/hyperlink/Hyperlink.tsx#L272)). A clean split would be:

   - Ctrl+K **while editing text** opens your new prompt box.
   - Ctrl+K **otherwise** keeps the current behavior.

   That requires catching the key in [textWysiwyg.tsx](packages/excalidraw/wysiwyg/textWysiwyg.tsx) before the app-level shortcut sees it. You'll want to confirm which one fires first while a text box is being edited.

2. **The existing `link` field can't hold your links.** It stores one URL for the whole element. Google Docs-style links mean a text box can contain several links, each covering certain characters. So you'd add a new field, for example:
   ```ts
   textLinks: {
     start: number;
     end: number;
     url: string;
   }
   [];
   ```
   That's an addition, not a change to existing behavior. The existing link UI keeps working as before.

**Other things your design brings in:**

- **The text editor is a plain `<textarea>`.** It can't show colored or underlined text, so links would only look like links after you finish editing. Making them visible while editing means replacing the textarea with a rich editor, which would push this well past "medium" scope.
- **Positions shift when text changes.** If the user types before a link, its `start`/`end` move. Every edit has to update the positions, or the link drifts onto the wrong characters. This is the trickiest part of the design.
- **Saving, loading and collaboration.** A new field needs default values when loading older files ([restore.ts](packages/excalidraw/data/restore.ts)). It also needs a check that it syncs correctly in collaborative sessions.
- **The prompt box** is a new component. You can model it on [ElementLinkDialog.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/ElementLinkDialog.tsx) and reuse the URL checks in [url.ts](packages/common/src/url.ts).

That fits the Option B file list from before, plus the new prompt component and the `textLinks` field.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-06 01:33:42Z)**_

Yes. Today every element, text boxes included, can hold at most one link, in the `link` field. That link belongs to the whole element and isn't tied to any characters:

- You add it with Ctrl+K or the context menu.
- A small link icon appears at the element's corner, and you click that icon (or the element in view mode) to open the URL.
- If you type or paste a URL into a text box today, it's just plain text. It isn't clickable and isn't connected to the `link` field.

So nothing in the codebase currently supports links inside text.

**To help you decide:**

|  | Option A (whole box is the link) | Option B (inline, like Google Docs) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Links per text box | 1 | Many |
| Custom display text | Yes, the box's text _is_ the display text | Yes |
| New field needed | No, reuses `link` | Yes (`textLinks`) |
| Hard parts | Mostly just paste and click handling | Finding links after line wrapping, click detection, positions shifting during edits |
| Fits "medium" scope | Under it | About right, if styling while editing is left out |

A cheaper version of your Google Docs flow is also possible: Ctrl+K while editing opens your prompt, and confirming creates a **separate** text element with that display text and its `link` set. That gets the "type a label, attach a URL" experience on top of Option A's existing plumbing. The tradeoff is that the link can't sit in the middle of a sentence.

_**User (2026-10-06 01:45:59Z)**_

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-06 01:46:07Z)**_

No. Links inside a sentence would be a **separate system alongside** the existing link logic, not a rework of it. The existing `link` field, its popup, its corner icon and the element-to-element links can all stay as they are.

The code that has to grow is the **text pipeline**:

- **Storage:** a new `textLinks` field on text elements.
- **Editing:** the Ctrl+K prompt, plus updating link positions as the user types.
- **Drawing:** styling the linked characters.
- **Clicking:** working out which characters were clicked once the text has wrapped, and opening that URL.

**Where the two systems meet** (design decisions, not rework):

1. **A text box with both kinds of link.** Nothing stops an element from having a whole-element `link` _and_ inline links. You'll need to decide which one wins on click: probably the inline link when the click lands on it, otherwise the existing behavior. You could also block having both.
2. **Ctrl+K:** as discussed, it opens your new prompt only while editing text and keeps the old behavior otherwise. That's a small branch, not a rewrite.
3. **Text inside shapes.** Text can be bound inside a rectangle or other shape and wraps to fit it. Your click detection has to handle that wrapping, but it can reuse the existing wrapping code rather than changing it.

In short, you'd extend the text system and leave the link system alone, apart from those two small decisions about how they coexist.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-06 02:02:13Z)**_

That plan holds together. Here's the scope as decided, followed by the questions still open.

**Decided**

- Pressing Ctrl+K while editing a text box opens a new dialog for the display text and URL.
- On confirm, the display text is inserted and a link entry is recorded for those characters.
- Links are stored in a new field on text elements, separate from the existing `link` field.
- Outside the text editor, Ctrl+K keeps its current behavior.

**Files in scope**

_New_

- A dialog component, e.g. `packages/excalidraw/components/TextLinkDialog.tsx` plus a `.scss` file. [ElementLinkDialog.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/ElementLinkDialog.tsx) is a good model.

_The new field_

- [packages/element/src/types.ts](packages/element/src/types.ts): add the field to the text element type.
- [packages/element/src/newElement.ts](packages/element/src/newElement.ts): default it to empty.
- [packages/excalidraw/data/restore.ts](packages/excalidraw/data/restore.ts): fill it in when loading older files.

**1. Ctrl+click to open**

- Use the codebase's existing cross-platform check (`event[KEYS.CTRL_OR_CMD]`) so it becomes Cmd+click on Mac.
- Ctrl/Cmd+click may already do something on the canvas, such as selecting or holding off snapping. Check `handleCanvasPointerDown` in [App.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx) and make the link check run first, only when the click lands on a link.

- **Typing inside a link** (inserting, not deleting): does that also remove the link? Treating any change to its characters as removal keeps the rule consistent.

- **Undo while editing:** the editing box's built-in Ctrl+Z restores the characters but not your link entry, so the text comes back as plain text. _**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-06 02:32:21Z)**_

Noted. I've recorded 3a and 3b as two candidates you're still choosing between. Let me know if 3b replaces 3a.

**3b: links grow and shrink as you edit** This feels more natural to use, but the bookkeeping is heavier. On each edit:

- **Insert inside the link, or right at its start or end, with no spaces:** the link grows.
- **Insert anywhere else:** links after the edit shift by the length of the insert.
- **Delete:** the link shrinks by however many of its characters were removed. When it reaches zero length, drop the entry.

Gaps to close:

- **A space typed _inside_ a link** (not at its edge): does it split the link, extend it, or end it there?
- **Pasting** a block of text that contains a space next to a link: does any of it get added to the link?
- **Typing in the gap between two links:** two adjacent links could both claim the same new character. You need a tie-break rule, such as "extend the link on the left".

The textarea only reports the text before and after each edit, so for each edit you'd compare the old and new text to work out what changed and where. 3a needs the same comparison, but its result is simpler to apply.

**5: Blue by default, with an option to use the text color**

- Text elements have **one color for the whole box** (`strokeColor`). Changing the text color in the properties panel recolors everything at once, and there's no per-character color.
- So each link entry needs its own color setting, for example `color: "link" | "inherit"`:
  - `"link"`: blue, regardless of the text color.
  - `"inherit"`: follows `strokeColor`, so recoloring the text recolors the link too.
- Getting the current text color for the dialog is easy. The element is right there while editing, so `element.strokeColor` is available immediately.
- **Underline:** the drawing API has no underline. You'd draw a line under each link, using the measured link positions you already need for clicking.

**6: Links simply coexist** No changes to the existing `link` logic are needed. The existing link is opened through its corner icon, and inline links only respond to Ctrl+click on their own characters, so the two don't compete.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-06 02:38:16Z)**_

Recorded. I've taken this to mean 3b is the final choice. Here's the full editing rule:

| Edit | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Insert strictly **inside** a link (any characters: spaces, paste, etc.) | Link grows |
| Insert at a link's **start or end**, with no spaces | Link grows |
| Insert a **space** at a link's start or end | Link unchanged; the space is plain text |
| Insert at the boundary **between two adjacent links** | The left link grows |
| Delete characters from a link | Link shrinks; removed at length 0 |
| Any edit before a link | Link shifts by the change in length |

Three small edge cases are left. Each has a sensible default, so they don't block you:

- **Pasting at a link's edge when the paste contains spaces** (e.g. pasting `foo bar` right after a link): default to treating it like typing, so it extends only if the paste starts with a non-space character.
- **Pressing Enter inside a link:** by your rule it extends the link, so links can span lines. The underline and click detection already have to handle wrapped lines, so this adds little work.
- **Replacing a selection that overlaps a link** (select some text and type over it): treat it as a delete followed by an insert, so the rules above apply in order.

That covers every design decision from the list. The scope and file list from earlier still stand. The editing logic lives mostly in [textWysiwyg.tsx](packages/excalidraw/wysiwyg/textWysiwyg.tsx), and it's worth writing as a standalone, pure function that takes the old text, new text and links and returns the updated links. That keeps it easy to unit-test against the table above.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-06 02:42:10Z)**_

I'd keep it in this issue. The underline is the cheap part once the rest is built.

**Why it's cheap:** to support Ctrl+click you already need the on-screen rectangle of each piece of a link, one per wrapped line. With those rectangles, the underline is a single short line drawn along the bottom of each one, roughly 10–15 lines of code in [renderElement.ts](packages/element/src/renderElement.ts). The hard work, mapping character positions to positions on screen through line wrapping, is shared with click detection.

**The bigger rendering cost is the blue color.** Each line of text is currently drawn in one call with one color. A blue link mid-sentence means drawing each line in pieces, one per color, and measuring each piece to know where the next starts. If anything is a candidate to split off, it's that, not the underline.

**What I'd split off instead:** links in **SVG export** ([staticSvgScene.ts](packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticSvgScene.ts)). That path builds text differently and needs its own colored pieces, underline and clickable `<a>` tags. It's self-contained and not needed for the user story.

**If you do want a temporary fallback** (for example, if splitting lines into colored pieces slips), the simplest one is **underline only, no color**. You'd draw lines under the link rectangles and leave the text drawing untouched. That still marks the link visually and needs nothing beyond the click-detection work.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-06 02:43:06Z)**_

By "link rectangles" I mean the boxes on screen where a link's characters are drawn. Here's what that means and why they matter.

**The problem:** your new field stores links by **character position**, e.g. "characters 10 to 25 are a link to google.com". But when someone Ctrl+clicks, the browser gives you a **screen position** (x, y in pixels). To know whether the click hit the link, you have to turn "characters 10–25" into "this area of the screen".

**Wrapping adds a complication.** A link might start at the end of one line and continue onto the next:

```
┌────────────────────────────────┐
│ Check out the docs at [Google  │  ← link part 1
│ Search] for more info.         │  ← link part 2
└────────────────────────────────┘
```

So one link can cover **two areas**:

```
                      ┌────────┐
 Check out the docs at│ Google │
┌────────┐            └────────┘
│ Search │ for more info.
└────────┘
```

Each of those boxes is a "link rectangle": an x, y, width and height covering one line's worth of a link's characters.

**How they get used:**

- **Ctrl+click:** check whether the click point falls inside any rectangle. If it does, open that link's URL.
- **Underline:** draw a line along the bottom edge of each rectangle.
- **Blue color:** draw the text inside each rectangle in blue.

So computing the rectangles is the core work, and the click, underline and color features all build on it. That's why I said the underline is cheap: once the rectangles exist, it's just a line along the bottom of each one.

**How you'd compute them:** the existing wrapping code ([textWrapping.ts](packages/element/src/textWrapping.ts)) already decides which characters land on which line. For each line, you'd measure the width of the text _before_ the link to get its left edge, and the width of the link text itself to get its width. [textMeasurements.ts](packages/element/src/textMeasurements.ts) already has helpers for measuring text width.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-06 02:44:46Z)**_

A hand-drawn underline can look like a traditional one. Browsers draw underlines the same way: a line placed relative to the text's baseline. In Excalidraw you have everything needed to do the same.

**Where it goes:** the text drawing code ([renderElement.ts:670-676](packages/element/src/renderElement.ts#L670-L676)) draws each line at `index * lineHeightPx + verticalOffset`. That y value is the line's **baseline**, the invisible line letters sit on. A traditional underline is:

- **Position:** slightly below the baseline, about `fontSize * 0.1`.
- **Thickness:** proportional to font size, about `fontSize * 0.06`, so it scales with the text.
- **Color:** the same as the link text, so it follows your blue/inherit setting.
- **Extent:** across the link's characters, spaces included, which is what Word and Google Docs do.

It's drawn on the same canvas context as the text, so it automatically moves, zooms, rotates and fades with the element.

**What you won't get for free:** browsers break the underline around letters that hang below the line, like g, y, p and j. This is called "skip-ink". Canvas can't do that natively, and imitating it means measuring each letter's shape, which is noticeably more work. Google Docs doesn't do skip-ink either; its underlines run straight through descenders. So a solid line is already the Google Docs look, and I'd skip it.

**Recommendation:** keep the underline in this issue with no temporary fallback. If anyone later wants skip-ink, make that a separate follow-up issue.

**Something I noticed while checking this:** `element.text` (what gets drawn) is the **already-wrapped** text, with extra line breaks added. `element.originalText` is what the user typed. Link positions should be stored against `originalText`, which is what the textarea edits. Then they need converting to wrapped-text positions when drawing. That conversion belongs to the link-rectangle work, not the underline, but it's an easy thing to get wrong.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-06 02:46:21Z)**_

Yes, split it off. Underline and bold for text in general is a different and bigger feature than hyperlinks, and it shouldn't block your issue.

**First, decide which kind of formatting the new issue means.**

|  | Whole text box (like changing font size) | Per character (like Google Docs) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Example | The entire text box is bold | Only some words are bold |
| Storage | Two new properties on the element (`bold`, `underline`) | Ranges, like your `textLinks` |
| UI | Toggles in the properties panel, next to font family and size | Ctrl+B / Ctrl+U in the text editor |
| Difficulty | Small to medium | Large |

**Problems specific to bold:**

- **The fonts have no bold versions.** Excalifont, Nunito, Lilita, Comic Shanns and others only ship as Regular in [packages/excalidraw/fonts/](packages/excalidraw/fonts/). Only Assistant has a Bold file. The browser can fake bold by thickening the letters, but faked bold can look different between browsers and in exports. Real bold means adding font files.
- **Bold text is wider, so it changes wrapping.** Text width is measured from a font string that has no weight ([utils.ts:110-118](packages/common/src/utils.ts#L110-L118)), so measuring, wrapping, the editing box and export would all need to know about bold. With per-character bold, a single line has mixed widths, which makes the wrapping code considerably harder.

Underline doesn't have these problems. It never changes text width, which is why it fits inside your hyperlink issue.

**How it relates to your hyperlink work:**

- Keep the hyperlink underline **in your issue**, drawn as discussed.
- If the formatting issue ends up per character, it will need the same parts you're building: character ranges, updating them on each edit, link rectangles and drawing in pieces. So a cheap way to future-proof is to write the range-update function and the rectangle calculation **generically**, so they work on "a range with some data" rather than specifically on links. The formatting issue could then reuse them instead of duplicating them.
- Later, the general underline feature and link underlines can share one drawing function.

I'd file it as its own issue: "Text formatting: bold and underline". Note the open choice between whole-box and per-character formatting, and the missing bold font files.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-06 02:47:20Z)**_

Yes, with one caveat about what you see while typing.

**Under each character:** the underline is drawn as one continuous line per line of the link, not one small line per character. It still runs under every character of the link, spaces included, and stops exactly where the link's text starts and ends. Because the measurements use the same font as the text itself, it lines up with the characters.

**As things move:** it isn't stored anywhere; it's recomputed from the current text and links every time the element is drawn. So it stays correct through:

- **Moving, zooming, rotating and resizing:** it's drawn on the same canvas as the text, so it gets the same transforms.
- **Re-wrapping**, when a text box or its container is resized: the link rectangles are recalculated, so the underline follows the link onto its new lines.
- **Left, center or right alignment:** the line positions account for alignment, the same way the text does.
- **Edits that grow or shrink the link** (your 3b rules): the link ranges update, and the next draw reflects them.

**Two things to get right for this to hold:**

1. **Bump the element's version when links change.** Excalidraw caches each element's drawing and only redraws when the element's version changes. If you update `textLinks` without going through the normal element-update path (`mutateElement` / `scene.mutateElement`), the old underline stays on screen.
2. **Not visible while typing.** During editing, the canvas text is hidden and the user types in a plain textarea, which can't show underlines or blue text. Links appear as soon as editing ends. Showing them while typing would mean replacing the textarea with a rich editor, which is out of scope, as we discussed.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-06 02:51:08Z)**_

Agreed, as a **text-editor feature**. User-applied underline (Ctrl+U, a toolbar toggle, underlining any text) brings in its own storage, shortcuts, UI, editing rules, export handling and collaboration concerns. That's a real widening of scope, and it isn't part of this issue.

What's in this issue is narrower: the underline is just **how a link looks**, the same as the blue color. Users can't apply or remove it on its own. It only exists where a link exists and is drawn from the link rectangles you already need for Ctrl+click. So it adds a small amount of drawing code, not a formatting feature.

If you'd rather keep even that out, links can be shown with color only. Ctrl+click and everything else would work the same.

```text
391	/**
392	 * Wraps the original text into the lines based on the given width.
393	 *
394	 * This is a convenience adapter over `getWrappedTextLines()` for call sites
395	 * that only need the rendered wrapped string and not the source offsets.
396	 */
397	export const wrapText = (
398	  text: string,
399	  font: FontString,
400	  maxWidth: number,
401	): string => {
402	  return getWrappedTextLines(text, font, maxWidth)
403	    .map((line) => line.text)
404	    .join("\n");
405	};
406
407	/**
408	 * A single rendered visual line produced from the original text.
409	 *
410	 * `start` and `end` are end-exclusive code-unit offsets into the original text, and do
411	 * not include synthetic soft line breaks inserted by this module. If trailing whitespace
412	 * was trimmed away at a wrap boundary, `end` points to the last rendered character.
413	 */
414	export type WrappedTextLine = {
415	  text: string;
416	  start: number;
417	  end: number;
418	};
419
420	/**
421	 * Splits only on existing hard line breaks and preserves original offsets.
422	 */
423	const getHardLineBreaks = (text: string): WrappedTextLine[] => {
424	  let offset = 0;
425
426	  return text.split("\n").map((line) => {
427	    const start = offset;
428	    const end = start + line.length;
429
430	    offset = end + 1;
431
432	    return {
433	      text: line,
434	      start,
435	      end,
436	    };
437	  });
438	};
439
440	/**
441	 * Returns the rendered visual lines together with their source offsets.
442	 *
443	 * This is the source-of-truth wrapping pipeline for callers that need more than the
444	 * final wrapped string, for example caret placement or future editor/rich-text mapping.
445	 */
446	export const getWrappedTextLines = (
447	  text: string,
448	  font: FontString,
449	  maxWidth: number,
450	): WrappedTextLine[] => {
451	  // if maxWidth is not finite or NaN which can happen in case of bugs in
452	  // computation, we need to make sure we don't continue as we'll end up
453	  // in an infinite loop
454	  if (!Number.isFinite(maxWidth) || maxWidth < 0) {
455	    return getHardLineBreaks(text);
456	  }
457
458	  const lines: WrappedTextLine[] = [];
459	  let offset = 0;
460
461	  for (const originalLine of text.split("\n")) {
462	    const originalLineWidth = getLineWidth(originalLine, font);
463
464	    if (originalLineWidth <= maxWidth) {
465	      lines.push({
466	        text: originalLine,
467	        start: offset,
468	        end: offset + originalLine.length,
469	      });
470	    } else {
471	      lines.push(...wrapLine(originalLine, font, maxWidth, offset));
472	    }
473
474	    offset += originalLine.length + 1;
475	  }
476
477	  return lines;
478	};
```

```text
export const newTextElement = (
  opts: {
    text: string;
    originalText?: string;
    fontSize?: number;
    fontFamily?: FontFamilyValues;
    textAlign?: TextAlign;
    verticalAlign?: VerticalAlign;
    containerId?: ExcalidrawTextContainer["id"] | null;
    lineHeight?: ExcalidrawTextElement["lineHeight"];
    autoResize?: ExcalidrawTextElement["autoResize"];
  } & ElementConstructorOpts,
): NonDeleted<ExcalidrawTextElement> => {
  const fontFamily = opts.fontFamily || DEFAULT_FONT_FAMILY;
  const fontSize = opts.fontSize || DEFAULT_FONT_SIZE;
  const lineHeight = opts.lineHeight || getLineHeight(fontFamily);
  const text = normalizeText(opts.text);
  const metrics = measureText(
    text,
    getFontString({ fontFamily, fontSize }),
    lineHeight,
  );
  const textAlign = opts.textAlign || DEFAULT_TEXT_ALIGN;
  const verticalAlign = opts.verticalAlign || DEFAULT_VERTICAL_ALIGN;
  const offsets = getTextElementPositionOffsets(
    { textAlign, verticalAlign },
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-06 03:25:28Z)**_

Yes, I'd rename it, and now is the cheapest time since nothing is committed yet.

The real ambiguity is that **"text link" can be read as "a link on a text element"**, and the existing `link` field already is that: a text element with a whole-element link. Someone reading `textLinks` next to `link` on a text element could reasonably wonder which is which. The codebase also already has `elementLink`, `ElementLinkDialog` and the `Hyperlink` component, so another "\*Link" name adds to the pile.

**My recommendation: `inlineLinks` / `InlineLink`.** "Inline" is the standard term for something that sits within a run of text, and it describes exactly what differs from the existing `link`: it's inside the text, not attached to the element. The planned names would follow:

| Current / planned         | Renamed              |
| ------------------------- | -------------------- |
| `textLinks` field         | `inlineLinks`        |
| `TextLink` type           | `InlineLink`         |
| `restoreTextLinks`        | `restoreInlineLinks` |

```typescript
import type { TextHyperlink } from "./types";

type TextChange = {
  /** offset in both texts at which the change starts */
  start: number;
  removedLength: number;
  inserted: string;
};

const isWhitespace = (char: string | undefined) => !!char && /\s/.test(char);

/** maps an offset in the old text to the new text after removing a range */
const shiftForRemoval = (
  offset: number,
  start: number,
  removedLength: number,
) => (offset <= start ? offset : Math.max(start, offset - removedLength));

/**
 * Finds the single contiguous change (removal + insertion) between two texts.
 *
 * Diffing alone is ambiguous when the edited characters match their
 * neighbours (e.g. typing "a" next to another "a"), so the caret position
 * after the edit, if supplied, is used to anchor the change.
 */
export const getTextChange = (
  oldText: string,
  newText: string,
  caret?: number,
): TextChange | null => {
  if (oldText === newText) {
    return null;
  }

  const minLength = Math.min(oldText.length, newText.length);

  let maxPrefix = minLength;
  if (caret !== undefined) {
    const insertedLength = Math.max(0, newText.length - oldText.length);
    maxPrefix = Math.min(maxPrefix, Math.max(0, caret - insertedLength));
  }

  let prefix = 0;
  while (prefix < maxPrefix && oldText[prefix] === newText[prefix]) {
    prefix++;
  }

  let suffix = 0;
  while (
    suffix < minLength - prefix &&
    oldText[oldText.length - 1 - suffix] ===
      newText[newText.length - 1 - suffix]
  ) {
    suffix++;
  }

  return {
    start: prefix,
    removedLength: oldText.length - prefix - suffix,
    inserted: newText.slice(prefix, newText.length - suffix),
  };
};

/**
 * Updates hyperlink ranges after the text was edited.
 *
 * - removed characters shrink the hyperlinks they belonged to, and
 *   hyperlinks that end up empty are dropped
 * - text inserted inside a hyperlink extends it
 * - text inserted at a hyperlink's edge extends it unless the character
 *   touching the hyperlink is whitespace
 * - when inserting between two adjacent hyperlinks, the left one wins
 * - hyperlinks after the change are shifted
 */
export const updateTextHyperlinks = (
  oldText: string,
  newText: string,
  textHyperlinks: readonly TextHyperlink[],
  caret?: number,
): readonly TextHyperlink[] => {
  if (!textHyperlinks.length) {
    return textHyperlinks;
  }

  const change = getTextChange(oldText, newText, caret);
  if (!change) {
    return textHyperlinks;
  }

  const { start: at, removedLength, inserted } = change;

  const shrunk = textHyperlinks
    .map((link) => ({
      ...link,
      start: shiftForRemoval(link.start, at, removedLength),
      end: shiftForRemoval(link.end, at, removedLength),
    }))
    .filter((link) => link.end > link.start);

  if (!inserted) {
    return shrunk;
  }

  const insertedLength = inserted.length;
  const extendsAtEnd = !isWhitespace(inserted[0]);
  const extendsAtStart = !isWhitespace(inserted[insertedLength - 1]);
  const leftHyperlinkExtends =
    extendsAtEnd && shrunk.some((link) => link.end === at);

  return shrunk.map((link) => {
    if (link.start < at && at < link.end) {
      return { ...link, end: link.end + insertedLength };
    }
    if (link.end === at && extendsAtEnd) {
      return { ...link, end: link.end + insertedLength };
    }
    if (link.start === at && extendsAtStart && !leftHyperlinkExtends) {
      return { ...link, end: link.end + insertedLength };
    }
    if (link.start >= at) {
      return {
        ...link,
        start: link.start + insertedLength,
        end: link.end + insertedLength,
      };
    }
    return link;
  });
};

/**
 * Replaces the selection with `displayText` and turns it into a hyperlink.
 *
 * Unlike regular typing, adjacent hyperlinks never extend over the inserted
 * text, and a hyperlink the selection is inside of is split around it.
 */
export const insertTextHyperlink = ({
  text,
  textHyperlinks,
  selectionStart,
  selectionEnd,
  displayText,
  url,
  color,
}: {
  text: string;
  textHyperlinks: readonly TextHyperlink[];
  selectionStart: number;
  selectionEnd: number;
  displayText: string;
  url: string;
  color: TextHyperlink["color"];
}): { text: string; textHyperlinks: TextHyperlink[] } => {
  const at = selectionStart;
  const removedLength = selectionEnd - selectionStart;
  const insertedLength = displayText.length;

  const nextHyperlinks: TextHyperlink[] = [];

  for (const link of textHyperlinks) {
    const start = shiftForRemoval(link.start, at, removedLength);
    const end = shiftForRemoval(link.end, at, removedLength);

    if (end <= start) {
      continue;
    }

    if (end <= at) {
      nextHyperlinks.push({ ...link, start, end });
    } else if (start >= at) {
      nextHyperlinks.push({
        ...link,
        start: start + insertedLength,
        end: end + insertedLength,
      });
    } else {
      nextHyperlinks.push({ ...link, start, end: at });
      nextHyperlinks.push({
        ...link,
        start: at + insertedLength,
        end: end + insertedLength,
      });
    }
  }

  if (insertedLength) {
    nextHyperlinks.push({ start: at, end: at + insertedLength, url, color });
  }

  nextHyperlinks.sort((a, b) => a.start - b.start);

  return {
    text:
      text.slice(0, selectionStart) + displayText + text.slice(selectionEnd),
    textHyperlinks: nextHyperlinks,
  };
};
```

```typescript
import {
  getTextChange,
  insertTextHyperlink,
  updateTextHyperlinks,
} from "../src/textHyperlinks";

import type { TextHyperlink } from "../src/types";

const link = (
  start: number,
  end: number,
  url = "https://excalidraw.com",
): TextHyperlink => ({ start, end, url, color: "link" });

/** returns the substrings covered by each hyperlink */
const linkedText = (text: string, links: readonly TextHyperlink[]) =>
  links.map((link) => text.slice(link.start, link.end));

/** simulates typing `inserted` at `at`, replacing `removedLength` chars */
const edit = (
  text: string,
  links: readonly TextHyperlink[],
  at: number,
  inserted: string,
  removedLength = 0,
) => {
  const nextText =
    text.slice(0, at) + inserted + text.slice(at + removedLength);
  const nextLinks = updateTextHyperlinks(
    text,
    nextText,
    links,
    at + inserted.length,
  );
  return { text: nextText, links: nextLinks };
};

describe("getTextChange", () => {
  it("returns null for identical texts", () => {
    expect(getTextChange("abc", "abc")).toBe(null);
  });

  it("detects an insertion", () => {
    expect(getTextChange("abc", "abXc")).toEqual({
      start: 2,
      removedLength: 0,
      inserted: "X",
    });
  });

  it("detects a removal", () => {
    expect(getTextChange("abcd", "ad")).toEqual({
      start: 1,
      removedLength: 2,
      inserted: "",
    });
  });

  it("detects a replacement", () => {
    expect(getTextChange("abcd", "aXYd")).toEqual({
      start: 1,
      removedLength: 2,
      inserted: "XY",
    });
```

**Two behaviors worth confirming, since the tests encode them:**

- **Pasting at a link's edge:** this applies the default I proposed earlier. At a link's end, the paste joins the link if its _first_ character isn't a space; at a link's start, if its _last_ character isn't a space. For example, pasting `foo bar` right after "Google" gives "Googlefoo bar", all linked.
- **Selecting all of a link's characters and typing over them** removes the link. Every character was deleted, so the new text is plain. Selecting only _part_ of a link and typing over it keeps the link.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-06 03:43:00Z)**_

That line is:

```ts
const isWhitespace = (char: string | undefined) => !!char && /\s/.test(char);
```

There's no "gEQ" in it. Here's each part, left to right:

**`(char: string | undefined) =>`**: the function takes one character, which may be `undefined`. That happens when the code asks for a character past the end of a string, e.g. `inserted[0]` on an empty string.

**`!!char`**: converts `char` to a true/false value.

- One `!` means "not", turning a value into a boolean and flipping it. `!"a"` is `false`, and `!undefined` is `true`.
- A second `!` flips it back. `!!"a"` is `true`, and `!!undefined` is `false`.

So `!!char` means "char exists and isn't an empty string".

**`&&`**: "and". It only evaluates the right side if the left side is true. If `char` is `undefined`, the function returns `false` straight away and never runs the test, so an undefined character counts as not whitespace.

**`/\s/`**: a regular expression, a pattern for matching text.

- The `/ ... /` slashes mark the start and end of the pattern, like quotes around a string.
- `\s` means "any whitespace character": space, tab, newline, and so on.

**`.test(char)`**: checks whether `char` matches the pattern, returning `true` or `false`.

**Read together:** "return true if `char` exists and is a whitespace character."

| `char`      | `!!char` | `/\s/.test(char)` | Result  |
| ----------- | -------- | ----------------- | ------- |
| `"a"`       | true     | false             | `false` |
| `" "`       | true     | true              | `true`  |
| `"\n"`      | true     | true              | `true`  |
| `undefined` | false    | _(skipped)_       | `false` |

okay so it's literlaly a long winded way of saying is whitespace i'm stupid mb.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-06 03:43:32Z)**_

Not stupid at all. `!!` and regex are both genuinely cryptic, and that line packs two of them together.

And yes, that's all it does: "is this a whitespace character?", plus a guard so a missing character returns `false` instead of erroring. Most of the length is the guard. Without it, `/\s/.test(undefined)` would test the string `"undefined"`, which happens to have no whitespace. That gives the right answer, but only by accident.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-06 03:48:24Z)**_

**Step 3: keep links updated while editing.** Step 2 built the rules. This step runs them live in the text editor and saves the result to the element. There's no visible change yet: links can't be created (step 4) or seen (step 5). But any links an element has will now follow the text correctly as the user types.

- [textWysiwyg.tsx](packages/excalidraw/wysiwyg/textWysiwyg.tsx): the editor keeps its own copy of the element's links. On every edit, it runs `updateTextHyperlinks` with the old text, new text and caret, then passes the updated links up along with the text. Tab and Shift+Tab indenting is handled separately, because indenting several lines edits several places at once and the comparison only handles one change.
- [App.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx): when the editor reports a change or submit, it saves `textHyperlinks` on the element alongside `originalText`.

```bash
describe("text hyperlinks", () => {
  const { h } = window;

  const hyperlink = (start: number, end: number) => ({
    start,
    end,
    url: "https://google.com",
    color: "link" as const,
  });

  const getTextHyperlinks = () =>
    (h.elements[0] as ExcalidrawTextElement).textHyperlinks;

  beforeEach(async () => {
    await render(<Excalidraw handleKeyboardGlobally={true} />);
    API.setElements([]);
  });

  /** opens the editor on "visit Google today" with "Google" hyperlinked */
  const openEditor = async () => {
    const text = API.createElement({
      type: "text",
      text: "visit Google today",
      x: 60,
      y: 0,
      width: 100,
      height: 100,
    });

    API.setElements([text]);
    API.updateElement(text, { textHyperlinks: [hyperlink(6, 12)] });
    API.setSelectedElements([text]);
    UI.clickTool("selection");

    Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.ENTER);

    return getTextEditor();
  };

  it("should keep hyperlinks in sync while typing", async () => {
    const editor = await openEditor();

    updateTextEditor(editor, "please visit Google today");
    expect(getTextHyperlinks()).toEqual([hyperlink(13, 19)]);

    updateTextEditor(editor, "please visit Gooogle today");
    expect(getTextHyperlinks()).toEqual([hyperlink(13, 20)]);
  });

  it("should persist hyperlinks when exiting the editor", async () => {
    const editor = await openEditor();

    updateTextEditor(editor, "please visit Google today");
    Keyboard.exitTextEditor(editor);

    expect(h.state.editingTextElement).toBeNull();
    expect(getTextHyperlinks()).toEqual([hyperlink(13, 19)]);
  });

  it("should drop hyperlinks whose text was deleted", async () => {
    const editor = await openEditor();

    updateTextEditor(editor, "visit  today");
    expect(getTextHyperlinks()).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("should shift hyperlinks when indenting and outdenting", async () => {
    const editor = await openEditor();

    editor.selectionStart = 0;
    editor.selectionEnd = 0;
    fireEvent.keyDown(editor, { key: KEYS.TAB });

    expect(editor.value).toBe(`${tab}visit Google today`);
    expect(getTextHyperlinks()).toEqual([hyperlink(10, 16)]);

    fireEvent.keyDown(editor, { key: KEYS.TAB, shiftKey: true });

    expect(editor.value).toBe("visit Google today");
    expect(getTextHyperlinks()).toEqual([hyperlink(6, 12)]);
  });
});
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-06 03:52:46Z)**_

Step 3 is done and not committed. It's tested, and the type check and lint pass.

**On your ordering question:** the order so far costs nothing, because steps 1–3 are small, separate and tested. I'd swap the next two, though: **drawing links before the dialog**, so you can see links (by loading a scene that already has them) before the dialog is built on top. Unless you say otherwise, the next step is drawing.

**Files changed (step 3):**

- [packages/excalidraw/wysiwyg/textWysiwyg.tsx](packages/excalidraw/wysiwyg/textWysiwyg.tsx):
  - The editor keeps its own copy of the links (`textHyperlinks`) and the text they match (`lastSyncedValue`).
  - `syncTextHyperlinks()` runs on every edit and before submitting.
  - Tab and Shift+Tab update links once per line.
  - `onChange` and `onSubmit` now pass the links along with the text.
- [packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx): `updateElement` saves `textHyperlinks` on the element. The `onSubmit` callback now unpacks its arguments on the line after its opening rather than in the parameter list. That keeps its body at its original indentation, so the diff stays small.
- [packages/excalidraw/wysiwyg/textWysiwyg.test.tsx](packages/excalidraw/wysiwyg/textWysiwyg.test.tsx): four new tests at the bottom, under `describe("text hyperlinks")`. They cover typing, saving on exit, deleting a link's text, and Tab/Shift+Tab.

**A bug the tests caught:** App wraps the editor callbacks in `withBatchedUpdates`, which only passes on the _first_ argument. My first version sent the links as a second argument, so they were silently lost while typing. `onChange` now sends one object, `{ nextOriginalText, nextTextHyperlinks }`, the same pattern `onSubmit` already used.

**Known gap:** links only update when text changes inside the editor. If something else changes `originalText` directly (for example, code that uses the library), links could end up out of range. Step 5's drawing code will skip out-of-range links rather than crash.

**Tests to run:**

1. `yarn test:update`. No snapshot changes are expected; App.tsx changes don't affect snapshots, since links are `[]` everywhere.
2. `yarn test:all`.

```
git add packages/excalidraw/wysiwyg/textWysiwyg.tsx packages/excalidraw/wysiwyg/textWysiwyg.test.tsx packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-06 04:14:04Z)**_

I fixed that failure, and the full suite now passes: 117 test files and 1,588 tests, with nothing failing. The type check and lint are clean.

**The cause was in my step 3 code.** `newElementWith`, which creates updated elements, treats any array value as a change, even if it's the exact same array. Because App passed `textHyperlinks` on every update, merely _opening_ the text editor replaced the element and bumped its version, even with no edits. That broke the test, since it holds a reference to the original element. It would also have added a pointless history and sync update every time a user opened a text box.

**The fix**, in [App.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx), inside `updateElement`: `textHyperlinks` is only included in the update when the links actually changed. Two empty lists count as unchanged, whether the field is `[]` or missing.

The files to stage are unchanged:

```

```

```bash
/** a run of text on a single rendered line, either plain or hyperlinked */
export type TextHyperlinkSegment = {
  text: string;
  /** x offset from the text element's left edge */
  x: number;
  width: number;
  hyperlink: TextHyperlink | null;
};

/**
 * Finds the offset of each rendered (wrapped) line in `originalText`.
 *
 * Wrapping only inserts line breaks and trims whitespace at wrap boundaries,
 * so each rendered line is a slice of the original text, in order.
 */
const getRenderedLineOffsets = (
  lines: readonly string[],
  originalText: string,
) => {
  const offsets: number[] = [];
  let cursor = 0;

  for (const line of lines) {
    const offset = originalText.indexOf(line, cursor);
    if (offset === -1) {
      return null;
    }
    offsets.push(offset);
    cursor = offset + line.length;
  }

  return offsets;
};

/**
 * Splits each rendered line of a text element into plain and hyperlinked
 * segments, positioned according to the element's text alignment.
 *
 * Returns `null` if the element has no hyperlinks, or if its rendered text
 * can't be mapped back to `originalText` (in which case hyperlinks are not
 * rendered rather than rendered in the wrong place).
 */
export const getTextHyperlinkLineSegments = (
  element: ExcalidrawTextElement,
): TextHyperlinkSegment[][] | null => {
  if (!element.textHyperlinks?.length) {
    return null;
  }

  const lines = element.text.replace(/\r\n?/g, "\n").split("\n");
  const offsets = getRenderedLineOffsets(lines, element.originalText);
  if (!offsets) {
    return null;
  }

  const font = getFontString(element);
  const hyperlinks = [...element.textHyperlinks].sort(
    (a, b) => a.start - b.start,
  );

  return lines.map((line, index) => {
    const lineStart = offsets[index];
    const lineEnd = lineStart + line.length;
    const lineWidth = getLineWidth(line, font);
    const lineX =
      element.textAlign === "center"
        ? (element.width - lineWidth) / 2
        : element.textAlign === "right"
        ? element.width - lineWidth
        : 0;

    const getX = (offset: number) =>
      lineX + (offset > 0 ? getLineWidth(line.slice(0, offset), font) : 0);

    const segments: TextHyperlinkSegment[] = [];
    const pushSegment = (
      start: number,
      end: number,
      hyperlink: TextHyperlink | null,
    ) => {
      const x = getX(start);
      segments.push({
        text: line.slice(start, end),
        x,
        width: getX(end) - x,
        hyperlink,
      });
    };

    let cursor = 0;
    for (const hyperlink of hyperlinks) {
      const start = Math.max(hyperlink.start, lineStart) - lineStart;
      const end = Math.min(hyperlink.end, lineEnd) - lineStart;
      if (end <= start || start < cursor) {
        continue;
      }
      if (start > cursor) {
        pushSegment(cursor, start, null);
      }
      pushSegment(start, end, hyperlink);
      cursor = end;
    }
    if (cursor < line.length || !segments.length) {
      pushSegment(cursor, line.length, null);
    }

    return segments;
  });
};
EOF
```

```bash
describe("getTextHyperlinkLineSegments", () => {
  const createTextElement = (
    opts: Partial<ExcalidrawTextElement> & { originalText: string },
  ): ExcalidrawTextElement => ({
    ...newTextElement({ text: opts.originalText, x: 0, y: 0 }),
    ...opts,
  });

  const widthOf = (element: ExcalidrawTextElement, text: string) =>
    getLineWidth(text, getFontString(element));

  /** strips positions to make assertions on the segment layout readable */
  const segmentTexts = (segments: ReturnType<typeof getTextHyperlinkLineSegments>) =>
    segments?.map((line) =>
      line.map((segment) => [segment.text, !!segment.hyperlink]),
    );

  it("returns null when there are no hyperlinks", () => {
    const element = createTextElement({ originalText: "visit Google" });
    expect(getTextHyperlinkLineSegments(element)).toBe(null);
  });

  it("splits a line into plain and hyperlinked segments", () => {
    const element = createTextElement({
      originalText: "visit Google today",
      textHyperlinks: [link(6, 12)],
    });
    const segments = getTextHyperlinkLineSegments(element)!;

    expect(segmentTexts(segments)).toEqual([
      [
        ["visit ", false],
        ["Google", true],
        [" today", false],
      ],
    ]);

    const [, hyperlinkSegment] = segments[0];
    expect(hyperlinkSegment.x).toBe(widthOf(element, "visit "));
    expect(hyperlinkSegment.width).toBe(
      widthOf(element, "visit Google") - widthOf(element, "visit "),
    );
  });

  it("maps hyperlinks onto wrapped lines", () => {
    const element = createTextElement({
      originalText: "visit Google today",
      // wrapping trims the spaces at the line breaks
      text: "visit\nGoogle\ntoday",
      textHyperlinks: [link(6, 12)],
    });

    expect(segmentTexts(getTextHyperlinkLineSegments(element))).toEqual([
      [["visit", false]],
      [["Google", true]],
      [["today", false]],
    ]);
  });

  it("splits a hyperlink spanning multiple lines", () => {
    const element = createTextElement({
      originalText: "foo bar",
      text: "foo\nbar",
      textHyperlinks: [link(1, 6)],
    });

    expect(segmentTexts(getTextHyperlinkLineSegments(element))).toEqual([
      [
        ["f", false],
        ["oo", true],
      ],
      [
        ["ba", true],
        ["r", false],
      ],
    ]);
  });

  it("offsets segments according to text alignment", () => {
    const element = createTextElement({
      originalText: "abc",
      textHyperlinks: [link(0, 3)],
      textAlign: "center",
      width: 1000,
    });
    const [[segment]] = getTextHyperlinkLineSegments(element)!;
    expect(segment.x).toBe((1000 - widthOf(element, "abc")) / 2);

    const rightAligned = { ...element, textAlign: "right" as const };
    const [[rightSegment]] = getTextHyperlinkLineSegments(rightAligned)!;
    expect(rightSegment.x).toBe(1000 - widthOf(element, "abc"));
  });

  it("ignores hyperlinks that are out of range", () => {
    const element = createTextElement({
      originalText: "abc",
      textHyperlinks: [link(1, 50)],
    });

    expect(segmentTexts(getTextHyperlinkLineSegments(element))).toEqual([
      [
        ["a", false],
        ["bc", true],
      ],
    ]);
  });

  it("returns null when the rendered text doesn't match the original text", () => {
    const element = createTextElement({
      originalText: "abc",
      text: "xyz",
```

Step 4 (drawing links) is written and not committed. The full suite passes (117 files, 1,595 tests), and the type check and lint are clean. I haven't seen it rendered in the app myself, so please use the sample scene below to check it visually.

**Files changed:**

- [packages/element/src/textHyperlinks.ts](packages/element/src/textHyperlinks.ts):
  - `TEXT_HYPERLINK_COLOR` is the palette's dark blue (`#1971c2`). `getTextHyperlinkColor` picks between it and the text's own color.
  - `getTextHyperlinkLineSegments(element)` splits each drawn line into plain and linked segments, each with its x position and width. It finds where each wrapped line sits in `originalText`, accounts for left, center and right alignment, and returns `null` (draw everything plainly) if the drawn text can't be matched to `originalText`. Click detection will reuse it.
- [packages/element/src/renderElement.ts](packages/element/src/renderElement.ts):
  - A new `drawTextHyperlinkLine` draws a line segment by segment. Linked segments get the link color and an underline about 0.1 × font size below the baseline, with a thickness of 0.06 × font size (at least 1px).
  - In the text drawing loop, lines with links use it; every other line draws exactly as before. Right-to-left text skips link styling.
- [packages/element/tests/textHyperlinks.test.ts](packages/element/tests/textHyperlinks.test.ts): 7 new tests for segment layout, covering a single line, wrapped lines, a link spanning two lines, center and right alignment, out-of-range links, and mismatched text.

The welcome screen means the canvas is empty, so the demo file hasn't been loaded into that window yet. The window `yarn start` opens always starts blank; you have to load the file into it.

**To load it**, use either option:

- **Menu → Open:** click ☰ at the top left, choose **Open**, then paste this full path into the file name box and press Enter:
  ```
  C:\Users\ab200\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\c--excalidraw\b25f2faf-70cf-402d-bc37-b273e3b0e278\scratchpad\hyperlinks-demo.excalidraw
  ```
  The folder is under the hidden `AppData` folder, so pasting the path is easier than browsing to it.
- **Drag and drop:** open that folder in File Explorer by pasting the folder part of the path into its address bar, then drag `hyperlinks-demo.excalidraw` onto the canvas.

**Two things to avoid:**

- Double-clicking the file in Explorer may open it on excalidraw.com, which doesn't have your changes.
- Make sure the tab's address is `localhost:3000`.

If loading it still shows the welcome screen, check whether an error message pops up, or whether the browser console (F12) shows red errors.

Here's how to drag the file in:

1. **Put the two windows side by side.** Keep the browser with `localhost:3000` open, then open File Explorer (Windows key + E).
2. **Go to the folder in File Explorer.** Click the address bar at the top, paste this, and press Enter:
   ```
   C:\Users\ab200\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\c--excalidraw\b25f2faf-70cf-402d-bc37-b273e3b0e278\scratchpad
   ```
3. **Arrange the windows.** Click the Explorer window and press Windows key + ←, then click the browser and press Windows key + →. Now both are visible.
4. **Drag the file.** In Explorer, press and hold the left mouse button on `hyperlinks-demo.excalidraw`, move the mouse over the white canvas in the browser, then release.

The scene should replace the welcome screen. If a box asks whether to replace the current content, confirm it.

If dragging is awkward, the Menu → Open route works too: click ☰ at the top left of the canvas, choose **Open**, paste the full file path (ending in `hyperlinks-demo.excalidraw`) into the **File name** box at the bottom of the dialog, and press Enter.

```text
export const Dialog = (props: DialogProps) => {
  const [islandNode, setIslandNode] = useCallbackRefState<HTMLDivElement>();
  const [lastActiveElement] = useState(document.activeElement);
  const { id } = useExcalidrawContainer();
  const isFullscreen = useEditorInterface().formFactor === "phone";

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!islandNode) {
      return;
    }

    const focusableElements = queryFocusableElements(islandNode);

    setTimeout(() => {
      if (focusableElements.length > 0 && props.autofocus !== false) {
        // If there's an element other than close, focus it.
        (focusableElements[1] || focusableElements[0]).focus();
      }
    });

    const handleKeyDown = (event: KeyboardEvent) => {
      if (event.key === KEYS.TAB) {
        const focusableElements = queryFocusableElements(islandNode);
        const { activeElement } = document;
        const currentIndex = focusableElements.findIndex(
          (element) => element === activeElement,
        );

        if (currentIndex === 0 && event.shiftKey) {
          focusableElements[focusableElements.length - 1].focus();
          event.preventDefault();
        } else if (
          currentIndex === focusableElements.length - 1 &&
          !event.shiftKey
        ) {
          focusableElements[0].focus();
          event.preventDefault();
        }
      }
    };

    islandNode.addEventListener("keydown", handleKeyDown);

    return () => islandNode.removeEventListener("keydown", handleKeyDown);
  }, [islandNode, props.autofocus]);

  const setAppState = useExcalidrawSetAppState();
  const setIsLibraryMenuOpen = useSetAtom(isLibraryMenuOpenAtom);

  const onClose = () => {
    setAppState({ openMenu: null });
    setIsLibraryMenuOpen(false);
    (lastActiveElement as HTMLElement).focus();
    props.onCloseRequest();
  };

  return (
    <Modal
      className={clsx("Dialog", props.className, {
        "Dialog--fullscreen": isFullscreen,
      })}
      labelledBy="dialog-title"
      maxWidth={getDialogSize(props.size)}
      onCloseRequest={onClose}
      closeOnClickOutside={props.closeOnClickOutside}
    >
      <Island ref={setIslandNode}>
        {props.title && (
          <h2 id={`${id}-dialog-title`} className="Dialog__title">
            <span className="Dialog__titleContent">{props.title}</span>
          </h2>
        )}
        {isFullscreen && (
          <button
            className="Dialog__close"
            onClick={onClose}
            title={t("buttons.close")}
            aria-label={t("buttons.close")}
            type="button"
          >
            {CloseIcon}
          </button>
        )}
        <div className="Dialog__content">{props.children}</div>
      </Island>
    </Modal>
  );
};
```

```typescript
import { useState } from "react";

import { KEYS, normalizeLink } from "@excalidraw/common";

import type { TextHyperlink } from "@excalidraw/element/types";

import { t } from "../i18n";

import { CheckboxItem } from "./CheckboxItem";
import { Dialog } from "./Dialog";
import DialogActionButton from "./DialogActionButton";
import { TextField } from "./TextField";

import "./TextHyperlinkDialog.scss";

import type { KeyboardEvent } from "react";

export type TextHyperlinkDialogResult = {
  displayText: string;
  url: string;
  color: TextHyperlink["color"];
};

/**
 * Dialog for inserting a hyperlink into the text being edited, opened via
 * Ctrl/Cmd+K from the text editor.
 */
export const TextHyperlinkDialog = ({
  initialDisplayText,
  onConfirm,
  onCancel,
}: {
  initialDisplayText: string;
  onConfirm: (result: TextHyperlinkDialogResult) => void;
  onCancel: () => void;
}) => {
  const [displayText, setDisplayText] = useState(initialDisplayText);
  const [url, setUrl] = useState("");
  const [useTextColor, setUseTextColor] = useState(false);

  const normalizedUrl = normalizeLink(url);

  const handleConfirm = () => {
    if (!normalizedUrl) {
      return;
    }
    onConfirm({
      // fall back to the URL itself when no text was provided
      displayText: displayText || url.trim(),
      url: normalizedUrl,
      color: useTextColor ? "inherit" : "link",
    });
  };

  const handleKeyDown = (event: KeyboardEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => {
    if (event.key === KEYS.ENTER) {
      event.preventDefault();
      handleConfirm();
    }
  };

  return (
    <Dialog
      size="small"
      onCloseRequest={onCancel}
      title={t("textHyperlinkDialog.title")}
      className="TextHyperlinkDialog"
    >
      <div className="TextHyperlinkDialog__fields">
        <TextField
          label={t("textHyperlinkDialog.displayText")}
          placeholder={t("textHyperlinkDialog.displayTextPlaceholder")}
          value={displayText}
          onChange={setDisplayText}
          onKeyDown={handleKeyDown}
          fullWidth
        />
        <TextField
          label={t("textHyperlinkDialog.url")}
          placeholder="https://"
          value={url}
          onChange={setUrl}
          onKeyDown={handleKeyDown}
          fullWidth
        />
        <CheckboxItem checked={useTextColor} onChange={setUseTextColor}>
          {t("textHyperlinkDialog.useTextColor")}
        </CheckboxItem>
      </div>
      <div className="TextHyperlinkDialog__actions">
        <DialogActionButton label={t("buttons.cancel")} onClick={onCancel} />
        <DialogActionButton
          label={t("buttons.confirm")}
          onClick={handleConfirm}
          actionType="primary"
          disabled={!normalizedUrl}
        />
      </div>
    </Dialog>
  );
};
```

```bash
cat >> packages/excalidraw/wysiwyg/textWysiwyg.test.tsx <<'EOF'

describe("text hyperlink dialog", () => {
  const { h } = window;

  const getTextElement = () => h.elements[0] as ExcalidrawTextElement;

  const getDialog = () =>
    document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(".TextHyperlinkDialog");

  const getDialogInputs = () => {
    const [displayTextInput, urlInput] = Array.from(
      getDialog()!.querySelectorAll("input"),
    );
    return { displayTextInput, urlInput };
  };

  const pressCtrlK = (editor: HTMLTextAreaElement) => {
    fireEvent.keyDown(editor, { key: KEYS.K, [KEYS.CTRL_OR_CMD]: true });
  };

  beforeEach(async () => {
    await render(<Excalidraw handleKeyboardGlobally={true} />);
    API.setElements([]);
  });

  const openEditor = async (text: string) => {
    const element = API.createElement({
      type: "text",
      text,
      x: 60,
      y: 0,
      width: 100,
      height: 100,
    });

    API.setElements([element]);
    API.setSelectedElements([element]);
    UI.clickTool("selection");

    Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.ENTER);

    return getTextEditor();
  };

  it("should open the dialog with the selected text prefilled", async () => {
    const editor = await openEditor("visit Google today");
    editor.setSelectionRange(6, 12);

    pressCtrlK(editor);

    expect(h.state.openDialog).toEqual({
      name: "textHyperlink",
      initialDisplayText: "Google",
    });
    expect(getDialogInputs().displayTextInput.value).toBe("Google");
    // still editing underneath the dialog
    expect(h.state.editingTextElement?.id).toBe(getTextElement().id);
  });

  it("should insert a hyperlink on confirm", async () => {
    const editor = await openEditor("visit  today");
    editor.setSelectionRange(6, 6);

    pressCtrlK(editor);

    const { displayTextInput, urlInput } = getDialogInputs();
    fireEvent.change(displayTextInput, { target: { value: "Google" } });
    fireEvent.change(urlInput, { target: { value: "https://google.com" } });
    fireEvent.click(queryByText(getDialog()!, "Confirm")!);

    expect(h.state.openDialog).toBe(null);
    expect(editor.value).toBe("visit Google today");
    expect(getTextElement().originalText).toBe("visit Google today");
    expect(getTextElement().textHyperlinks).toEqual([
      { start: 6, end: 12, url: "https://google.com", color: "link" },
    ]);
    // the editor stays open with the caret after the inserted text
    expect(h.state.editingTextElement?.id).toBe(getTextElement().id);
    expect(editor.selectionStart).toBe(12);
  });

  it("should use the text color when the checkbox is checked", async () => {
    const editor = await openEditor("visit Google today");
    editor.setSelectionRange(6, 12);

    pressCtrlK(editor);

    const { urlInput } = getDialogInputs();
    fireEvent.change(urlInput, { target: { value: "https://google.com" } });
    fireEvent.click(queryByText(getDialog()!, "Use text color")!);
    fireEvent.keyDown(urlInput, { key: KEYS.ENTER });

    expect(getTextElement().textHyperlinks).toEqual([
      { start: 6, end: 12, url: "https://google.com", color: "inherit" },
    ]);
  });

  it("should use the URL as the text when no text is given", async () => {
    const editor = await openEditor("visit ");
    editor.setSelectionRange(6, 6);

    pressCtrlK(editor);

    const { urlInput } = getDialogInputs();
    fireEvent.change(urlInput, { target: { value: "https://google.com" } });
    fireEvent.keyDown(urlInput, { key: KEYS.ENTER });

    expect(editor.value).toBe("visit https://google.com");
    expect(getTextElement().textHyperlinks).toEqual([
      { start: 6, end: 24, url: "https://google.com", color: "link" },
    ]);
  });

  it("should not confirm without a URL", async () => {
    const editor = await openEditor("visit Google today");
    editor.setSelectionRange(6, 12);

    pressCtrlK(editor);
    fireEvent.click(queryByText(getDialog()!, "Confirm")!);

    expect(h.state.openDialog?.name).toBe("textHyperlink");
    expect(getTextElement().textHyperlinks).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("should keep editing unchanged text when cancelled", async () => {
    const editor = await openEditor("visit Google today");
    editor.setSelectionRange(6, 12);

    pressCtrlK(editor);
    fireEvent.click(queryByText(getDialog()!, "Cancel")!);

    expect(h.state.openDialog).toBe(null);
    expect(editor.value).toBe("visit Google today");
    expect(getTextElement().textHyperlinks).toEqual([]);
    expect(h.state.editingTextElement?.id).toBe(getTextElement().id);
  });
});
EOF
```

The Ctrl+K dialog (step 5) works and isn't committed. On a clean re-run, the full suite passed: 117 test files and 1,601 tests. The type check, lint and Prettier checks pass too, and I tried it in Chrome.

**About the 18 failures you might have seen:** my first full run failed 18 tests. I started it while my dev server was still shutting down, and each failure was the first test in its file. The one file I re-ran on its own passed, and the full suite passed when run again by itself. If you see the same thing, re-run it.

**How it behaves:**

- Ctrl/Cmd+K while editing text opens an "Insert link" dialog. Any selected text pre-fills the Text field, and the dialog has a Link field and a "Use text color" checkbox.
- Confirm (or Enter in either field) replaces the selection with the text and makes it a link. The editor stays open with the caret after the link.
- If Text is empty, the URL itself becomes the text.
- Confirm is disabled until a URL is entered.
- Cancel or Escape closes the dialog and returns you to the text unchanged.
- Outside the text editor, Ctrl+K still opens the existing whole-element link editor.

**Files changed:**

- [TextHyperlinkDialog.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/TextHyperlinkDialog.tsx) (new): the dialog, built from the existing `Dialog`, `TextField`, `CheckboxItem` and `DialogActionButton` components. URLs go through `normalizeLink`, which blocks `javascript:` links.
- [TextHyperlinkDialog.scss](packages/excalidraw/components/TextHyperlinkDialog.scss) (new): layout only.
- [textWysiwyg.tsx](packages/excalidraw/wysiwyg/textWysiwyg.tsx):
  - Ctrl+K handling stops the app's own Ctrl+K from also firing.
  - `openTextHyperlinkDialog` pauses submit-on-blur and inserts the link on confirm.
  - The editor no longer steals focus from the dialog, and closing the editor also closes the dialog.
- [App.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx):
  - `openTextHyperlinkDialog`/`closeTextHyperlinkDialog` pass the result back to the editor.
  - Keyboard shortcuts are paused while the dialog is open, so Escape can't close the text editor underneath it.
  - If something else replaces the dialog, the editor is told it was cancelled.
- [LayerUI.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/LayerUI.tsx): renders the dialog.
- [types.ts](packages/excalidraw/types.ts): the `"textHyperlink"` dialog type, and `closeTextHyperlinkDialog` added to `AppClassProperties`.
- [en.json](packages/excalidraw/locales/en.json): a new `textHyperlinkDialog` section with the labels.
- [textWysiwyg.test.tsx](packages/excalidraw/wysiwyg/textWysiwyg.test.tsx): six new tests under `describe("text hyperlink dialog")` covering pre-fill, confirm, use-text-color, the URL fallback, blocked confirm without a URL, and cancel.

```bash
/**
 * Returns the hyperlink rendered under the given scene point, if any.
 */
export const getTextHyperlinkAtPoint = (
  element: ExcalidrawTextElement,
  point: GlobalPoint,
  elementsMap: ElementsMap,
): TextHyperlink | null => {
  const lineSegments = getTextHyperlinkLineSegments(element);
  if (!lineSegments) {
    return null;
  }

  const [x1, y1, , , cx, cy] = getElementAbsoluteCoords(element, elementsMap);
  const angle = getTextElementAngle(
    element,
    getContainerElement(element, elementsMap),
  );

  // undo the element's rotation so we can work in its local coordinates
  const [x, y] = pointRotateRads(
    point,
    pointFrom<GlobalPoint>(cx, cy),
    -angle as Radians,
  );
  const localX = x - x1;
  const localY = y - y1;

  const lineHeightPx = getLineHeightInPx(element.fontSize, element.lineHeight);
  const segments = lineSegments[Math.floor(localY / lineHeightPx)];
  if (!segments) {
    return null;
  }

  return (
    segments.find(
      (segment) =>
        segment.hyperlink &&
        localX >= segment.x &&
        localX <= segment.x + segment.width,
    )?.hyperlink ?? null
  );
};
EOF
```

```bash
describe("getTextHyperlinkAtPoint", () => {
  // "visit Google today" at (100, 100) with "Google" hyperlinked
  const createTextElement = (opts: Partial<ExcalidrawTextElement> = {}) => {
    const element = newTextElement({
      text: "visit Google today",
      x: 100,
      y: 100,
    });
    return {
      ...element,
      textHyperlinks: [link(6, 12)],
      ...opts,
    } as ExcalidrawTextElement;
  };

  const font = (element: ExcalidrawTextElement) => getFontString(element);

  /** scene x of the middle of "Google" */
  const getHyperlinkCenterX = (element: ExcalidrawTextElement) => {
    const start = getLineWidth("visit ", font(element));
    const end = getLineWidth("visit Google", font(element));
    return element.x + (start + end) / 2;
  };

  const hitTest = (element: ExcalidrawTextElement, x: number, y: number) =>
    getTextHyperlinkAtPoint(
      element,
      pointFrom<GlobalPoint>(x, y),
      arrayToMap([element]),
    );

  it("returns the hyperlink under the point", () => {
    const element = createTextElement();
    const y = element.y + element.height / 2;

    expect(hitTest(element, getHyperlinkCenterX(element), y)).toEqual(
      link(6, 12),
    );
  });

  it("returns null for plain text and points outside the element", () => {
    const element = createTextElement();
    const y = element.y + element.height / 2;

    // over "visit"
    expect(hitTest(element, element.x + 1, y)).toBe(null);
    // above and below the text
    expect(hitTest(element, getHyperlinkCenterX(element), element.y - 5)).toBe(
      null,
    );
    expect(
      hitTest(
        element,
        getHyperlinkCenterX(element),
        element.y + element.height + 5,
      ),
    ).toBe(null);
  });

  it("accounts for the element's rotation", () => {
    const element = createTextElement({ angle: Math.PI as Radians });
    const cx = element.x + element.width / 2;
    const y = element.y + element.height / 2;

    // rotating by 180° mirrors the text around its center
    const mirroredX = 2 * cx - getHyperlinkCenterX(element);
    expect(hitTest(element, mirroredX, y)).toEqual(link(6, 12));
    expect(hitTest(element, getHyperlinkCenterX(element), y)).toBe(null);
  });
});
EOF
```

Add Ctrl+click integration tests and run

```bash
cat > packages/excalidraw/tests/textHyperlinks.test.tsx <<'EOF'
import { getFontString } from "@excalidraw/common";
import { getLineWidth } from "@excalidraw/element";

import type { ExcalidrawTextElement } from "@excalidraw/element/types";

import { Excalidraw } from "../index";

import { API } from "./helpers/api";
import { Keyboard, Pointer } from "./helpers/ui";
import { render, unmountComponent } from "./test-utils";

import type { MockInstance } from "vitest";

unmountComponent();

const mouse = new Pointer("mouse");

describe("opening text hyperlinks", () => {
  const { h } = window;

  let windowOpen: MockInstance<typeof window.open>;

  beforeEach(() => {
    mouse.reset();
    windowOpen = vi
      .spyOn(window, "open")
      .mockReturnValue({ opener: null, location: "" } as unknown as Window);
  });

  afterEach(() => {
    windowOpen.mockRestore();
  });

  /** creates "visit Google today" with "Google" hyperlinked */
  const setup = () => {
    const text = API.createElement({
      type: "text",
      text: "visit Google today",
      x: 0,
      y: 0,
    }) as ExcalidrawTextElement;

    API.setElements([text]);
    API.updateElement(text, {
      textHyperlinks: [
        { start: 6, end: 12, url: "https://google.com", color: "link" },
      ],
    });

    const font = getFontString(text);
    const hyperlinkX =
      (getLineWidth("visit ", font) + getLineWidth("visit Google", font)) / 2;

    return { text, hyperlinkX, y: 5 };
  };

  it("should open the hyperlink on ctrl/cmd+click", async () => {
    await render(<Excalidraw handleKeyboardGlobally={true} />);
    const { hyperlinkX, y } = setup();

    Keyboard.withModifierKeys({ ctrl: true }, () => {
      mouse.clickAt(hyperlinkX, y);
    });

    expect(windowOpen).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(windowOpen).toHaveBeenCalledWith(undefined, "_blank");
    // the click opens the hyperlink instead of selecting the element
    expect(API.getSelectedElements()).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("should not open the hyperlink on a plain click", async () => {
    await render(<Excalidraw handleKeyboardGlobally={true} />);
    const { text, hyperlinkX, y } = setup();

    mouse.clickAt(hyperlinkX, y);

    expect(windowOpen).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(API.getSelectedElements().map((element) => element.id)).toEqual([
      text.id,
    ]);
  });

  it("should not open anything on ctrl/cmd+click outside hyperlinks", async () => {
    await render(<Excalidraw handleKeyboardGlobally={true} />);
    const { y } = setup();

    Keyboard.withModifierKeys({ ctrl: true }, () => {
      mouse.clickAt(1, y);
    });

    expect(windowOpen).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it("should let the host handle the hyperlink via onLinkOpen", async () => {
    const onLinkOpen = vi.fn((element, event) => {
      event.preventDefault();
    });
    await render(
      <Excalidraw handleKeyboardGlobally={true} onLinkOpen={onLinkOpen} />,
    );
    const { text, hyperlinkX, y } = setup();

    Keyboard.withModifierKeys({ ctrl: true }, () => {
      mouse.clickAt(hyperlinkX, y);
    });

    expect(onLinkOpen).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(onLinkOpen.mock.calls[0][0]).toMatchObject({
      id: text.id,
      link: "https://google.com",
    });
    expect(windowOpen).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(h.state.editingTextElement).toBe(null);
  });
});
EOF
```

Step 6 is done and not committed. The full suite passes (118 test files, 1,608 tests), and the type check and lint are clean. In Chrome:

- **A plain click on a link** selects the element as usual and opens nothing.
- **Ctrl+click on "Google"** opened `https://www.google.com/` in a new tab.
- **Ctrl+click on the wrapped link inside the box** opened `https://example.com/`.

**Files changed:**

- [textHyperlinks.ts](packages/element/src/textHyperlinks.ts): a new `getTextHyperlinkAtPoint(element, point, elementsMap)` at the bottom. It undoes the element's rotation, works out which line was clicked, and checks that line's segments from step 4. It uses the existing `getElementAbsoluteCoords`/`getTextElementAngle`, so text inside shapes and arrows is handled.
- [App.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx):
  - **Near the top of `handleCanvasPointerDown`:** a Ctrl/Cmd+click on a link while not editing opens it and stops there, so no selection or drag starts.
  - **`getTextHyperlinkAtPosition`:** finds the topmost text element with a link under the cursor.
  - **`openTextHyperlink`:** opens the URL with the same behavior as element links. It calls `onLinkOpen` for apps that embed Excalidraw, opens local links in the same tab, and sets `noopener`. It's a separate copy, so the existing link code is untouched, as you wanted.
- [packages/element/tests/textHyperlinks.test.ts](packages/element/tests/textHyperlinks.test.ts): 3 hit-test tests, covering a hit, misses, and a rotated element.
- [packages/excalidraw/tests/textHyperlinks.test.tsx](packages/excalidraw/tests/textHyperlinks.test.tsx) (new): 4 click tests. Ctrl+click opens the link, a plain click selects instead, Ctrl+click outside a link does nothing, and `onLinkOpen` can take over.

**Tests:** `yarn test:update`, then `yarn test:all`.

**Title:** `feat: inline hyperlinks in text elements`

```markdown
Closes #<issue>

## Summary

Adds Google Docs–style hyperlinks inside text elements. Links can sit mid-sentence, and one text box can contain several of them.

- **Create:** while editing text, press Ctrl/Cmd+K to open an "Insert link" dialog. It has text (pre-filled from the selection) and URL fields, plus a "Use text color" option.
- **Display:** links are drawn blue (or in the text's own color) and underlined. This works across wrapped lines, text alignment, rotation, and text inside shapes.
- **Open:** Ctrl/Cmd+click opens the link. A pointer cursor shows on Ctrl/Cmd+hover. A plain click still selects as usual.
- **Editing:** links grow when typing inside them or at their edges, except for spaces at an edge. They shrink on delete and are removed once empty. Between two adjacent links, the left link takes priority.

## Implementation

- New optional `textHyperlinks` field on text elements: `{ start, end, url, color }[]`, with offsets into `originalText`. Older files load with `[]`, and invalid entries are dropped.
- `packages/element/src/textHyperlinks.ts`: editing rules, line segment layout, hit testing.
- The existing whole-element `link` feature is unchanged. Outside the text editor, Ctrl+K still opens it.

## Not included

- Links in SVG export (they export as plain text)
- Right-to-left text shows links as plain text

## Testing

- Unit tests for the editing rules, segment layout, and hit testing
- Integration tests for editor syncing, the dialog, Ctrl/Cmd+click, `onLinkOpen`, and the cursor
- `yarn test:all` passes
- Checked manually in Chrome

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
```
