_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-06 06:04:18Z)**_

The branch adds one field and six types, in three groups.

### 1. Saved data (stored in `.excalidraw` files and synced in collaboration)

**`textHyperlinks` field on text elements:** [packages/element/src/types.ts](packages/element/src/types.ts)

```ts
textHyperlinks?: readonly TextHyperlink[];
```

- It's a list of the text box's links.
- It's **optional** (`?`), so old files and existing code that build text elements still type-check. New elements get `[]`, and loading a file fills in `[]` and drops invalid entries (`restoreTextHyperlinks` in [restore.ts](packages/excalidraw/data/restore.ts)).
- Positions count characters in `originalText`, what the user typed, not the wrapped `text` that's drawn.

**`TextHyperlink` type:** same file

```ts
type TextHyperlink = Readonly<{
  start: number; // first character of the link
  end: number; // one past the last character
  url: string;
  color: "link" | "inherit"; // blue, or the text's own color
}>;
```

For example, "Google" in `"visit Google today"` is `{ start: 6, end: 12, ... }`.

### 2. App state (in memory only, never saved)

**New `openDialog` option:** [packages/excalidraw/types.ts](packages/excalidraw/types.ts)

```ts
| { name: "textHyperlink"; initialDisplayText: string }
```

This is how the app knows the Ctrl+K dialog is open, and what text to pre-fill.

**`closeTextHyperlinkDialog` on `AppClassProperties`:** same file. It lets LayerUI tell App when the dialog closes, without LayerUI getting full access to App.

### 3. Internal types (code only, never saved)

| Type | File | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TextHyperlinkDialogResult` | [TextHyperlinkDialog.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/TextHyperlinkDialog.tsx) | What the dialog returns: `{ displayText, url, color }` |
| `TextHyperlinkSegment` | [textHyperlinks.ts](packages/element/src/textHyperlinks.ts) | One piece of a drawn line: `{ text, x, width, hyperlink }`, used by drawing and clicking |
| `TextChange` | [textHyperlinks.ts](packages/element/src/textHyperlinks.ts) | What one edit did: `{ start, removedLength, inserted }`. Private to that file |

Only group 1 affects saved files and other users. Groups 2 and 3 can be changed freely later without breaking anyone's drawings.

- **[textWysiwyg.tsx](packages/excalidraw/wysiwyg/textWysiwyg.tsx):** keeps links in sync while typing, handles Ctrl/Cmd+K, and opens the dialog.
- **[App.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx):**
  - Saves links when text is edited.

- **[restore.ts](packages/excalidraw/data/restore.ts):** `restoreTextHyperlinks` validates links when a file loads.
- **[newElement.ts](packages/element/src/newElement.ts):** new text elements start with `textHyperlinks: []`.
- **[en.json](packages/excalidraw/locales/en.json):** a `textHyperlinkDialog` section with the dialog's labels.

### User-facing behavior

- Ctrl/Cmd+K while editing text opens the "Insert link" dialog.
- Links are blue (or the text color) and underlined.
- Ctrl/Cmd+click opens a link, and Ctrl/Cmd+hover shows a pointer.

### Worth noting as limitations

- Links show as plain text in SVG export.
- Right-to-left text shows links as plain text.
- While you're typing in a text box, links aren't styled; they appear once editing ends.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-06 06:17:32Z)**_

Yes, for every text element created inside Excalidraw. All of them go through `newTextElement`: the text tool, double-clicking a shape, pasting, Mermaid conversion, and the `convertToExcalidrawElements` API. I checked for code that builds text elements another way, and the matches were only references in `boundElements` lists, test fixtures, or a demo file.

Other ways text elements show up:

- **Duplicates and copy-paste** copy the field from the original.
- **Files and shared scenes** get `[]` when loaded, via `restoreTextHyperlinks`.

**The one gap:** apps that embed Excalidraw can pass raw element objects straight into `updateScene` without the loading step, and those may have no field at all. That's why the field is optional (`?`), and why every piece of code reading it treats a missing field as "no links" (`?? []` and `?.length`). Nothing breaks in that case.
